blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: After the weekly funding LP is solved on an incremental GLOP solver, four edits are proposed, each to be re-solved on its own from that solve. Which edit is likely to need the most pivots?

options.text: Raising by 5% the NPV of a project the current plan leaves unfunded
options.says: A new objective coefficient leaves the old vertex allowed; at most a few pivots bring the project in.

options.text: Adding a cap on total carry-over far below what the plan carries now
options.says: Right: the old point breaks the new row by a lot, so many rows have to be repaired; in the lesson this took 116 of a cold solve's 189 pivots.

options.text: Adding a new candidate project that spends in two of the plan years
options.says: The old vertex stays allowed with the new share at 0; the lesson's new project took 4 pivots.

options.text: Lowering one year's budget by $100k out of a budget of $38,000k
options.says: A small change to a right-hand side keeps the old basis; the lesson's cut of 100 took 0 pivots.

origin.section: A Warm Start Survives Some Changes Better Than Others

questions.stem: A team will run 300 budget what-ifs of one large LP through MathOpt's IncrementalSolver with OR-Tools 9.15. On which solver should each what-if take far fewer iterations than a solve from scratch?

options.text: HiGHS, as its dual simplex restarts from the last basis it found
options.says: Measured in the lesson: HiGHS's re-solve through MathOpt took 22 iterations, the same as a cold solve.

options.text: PDLP, as its first-order steps restart from the last point it found
options.says: Measured in the lesson: PDLP's re-solve took 384 iterations, the same as a cold solve.

options.text: Any of the three, as IncrementalSolver keeps each solver's last answer
options.says: Whether the next solve starts from the last one depends on the solver; only GLOP's counts dropped.

options.text: GLOP, as its simplex restarts from the last basis it found
options.says: Right: GLOP re-solved the cut in 216 pivots against 4,660 from scratch.

origin.section: Not Every Solver Warm-Starts Through MathOpt

questions.stem: In a maximizing LP, a budget row has dual value 0.8 and the optimum is 10,000. Finance proposes cutting that budget by 3,000, far more than any cut tried before. What can you say before re-solving?

options.text: The optimum will be at most 7,600; a re-solve says how far below
options.says: Right: in a maximizing LP each further unit of budget is worth no more than the last, so the dual prediction is an upper bound.

options.text: The optimum will be 7,600, as the dual value is the rate of change
options.says: The rate holds only while the basis stays the same; a cut this large may pass where it changes.

options.text: The optimum will be at least 7,600, as later units are worth less
options.says: Units cut later are worth at least as much as the first, not less, so the loss can only exceed 2,400.

options.text: The optimum will be 7,000, as each unit cut loses one unit of value
options.says: The dual value, 0.8, is what a unit of budget is worth here, not 1.

origin.section: A Dual Value Predicts a Small Change; Re-Solve to Know a Large One
